title: TURKEY'S
10 LARGEST
PROVINCES

hook.say: Turkey's ten largest provinces, ranked. Number one is bigger than Belgium!

outro.say: Is your province on the list? Comment below!

outroLines: IS YOUR PROVINCE ON THE LIST?

items.name: Diyarbakır
items.say: Number ten: Dee-yarbakur, famous for its black city walls. 15,200 square kilometers.
items.cap: Number ten: Diyarbakır, famous for its black city walls. 15,200 square kilometers.

items.name: Mersin
items.say: Nine: Mairseen, with a long Mediterranean coast. 16,000 square kilometers.
items.cap: Nine: Mersin, with a long Mediterranean coast. 16,000 square kilometers.

items.name: Kayseri
items.say: Eight: Kyseri, home of Mount Air-jee-yes. 17,000 square kilometers.
items.cap: Eight: Kayseri, home of Mount Erciyes. 17,000 square kilometers.

items.name: Şanlıurfa
items.say: Seven: Shanluh-Urfa, home of the world's oldest temple. 19,200 square kilometers.
items.cap: Seven: Şanlıurfa, home of the world's oldest temple. 19,200 square kilometers.

items.name: Antalya
items.say: Six: Ahn-tahl-ya, Turkey's tourism capital. 20,200 square kilometers.
items.cap: Six: Antalya, Turkey's tourism capital. 20,200 square kilometers.

items.name: Van
items.say: Five: Vahn, with Turkey's largest lake. 20,900 square kilometers.
items.cap: Five: Van, with Turkey's largest lake. 20,900 square kilometers.

items.name: Erzurum
items.say: Four: Air-zoo-room, one of Turkey's highest cities. 25,000 square kilometers.
items.cap: Four: Erzurum, one of Turkey's highest cities. 25,000 square kilometers.

items.name: Ankara
items.say: Three: Ankara, the capital. 25,600 square kilometers.
items.cap: Three: Ankara, the capital. 25,600 square kilometers.

items.name: Sivas
items.say: Two: See-vahss, in the heart of Anatolia. 28,200 square kilometers.
items.cap: Two: Sivas, in the heart of Anatolia. 28,200 square kilometers.

items.name: Konya
items.say: And number one: Konya! 40,800 square kilometers, bigger than Belgium.
items.cap: And number one: Konya! 40,800 square kilometers, bigger than Belgium.
